question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a distance thrice its focal length (3f). The image is formed at:

options.text: a point between F and C

solution:
The correct answer is __**a point between F and C**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed at a distance of 3f (thrice the focal length) from a concave mirror, it forms an image between the focal point (F) and the center of curvature (C).
 
• The nature of the image formed is real, inverted, and smaller than the object.
 
• This principle is derived from the mirror equation and ray diagrams for concave mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
